method: EXTERNAL_RITUAL_CITATION. A named ritual text quotes the mantra by its pratika inside an instruction. Deliberately NOT proximity to ritual vocabulary, which GAP-RITUAL-006 records as circular, since the ritual vocabulary is the thing the context is meant to explain. Four precision controls: word-boundary anchoring; a two-word minimum span; the run must end where a citing word ends; and the span must be reproducible from a text form this graph stores for the mantra, which the fourth control adds here and which removes 25 of 769 EXACT rows.

values.EMPLOYED_IN_RITE: A named ritual work quotes this mantra by its pratika inside an instruction, the quotation is closed by `iti`, and the matched span is reproducible from a text form this graph stores for the mantra.
values.EMPLOYED_IN_RITE_PROBABLE: Reached by the same matcher, but the locus is PROBABLE, or is not closed by `iti`, or its span cannot be reproduced from any stored text form. Not asserted.
values.RITE_NAMED_IN_THIS_MANTRA: The mantra itself names a rite. A different claim from being employed in one.
values.UNRESOLVED_SHARED_OPENING: The mantra's opening letters are shared with at least one other mantra, so a quotation of that opening cannot be attributed to it. The rivals are named. This is NOT evidence of absence.
values.NO_RITUAL_CITATION_FOUND: Assessed against all 61,393 cited lines of the eighteen acquired ritual works and no quotation was found. This is NOT `non-ritual`: the mantra may be quoted in a work not acquired, or by a pratika shorter than the two-word minimum. No mantra anywhere in this artifact is marked NON_RITUAL, because nothing measured here could support that.

no_value_means_non_ritual: NO_RITUAL_CITATION_FOUND is a measured absence against the eighteen acquired works. It is not a finding that a mantra is non-ritual, and no mantra in this artifact carries NON_RITUAL.
